It would be very easy for him to just ask what the situation was on this date or that date in Sarajevo, rather than reading out a SRNA report and saying: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, I think he's conformed with your practice by establishing as a general matter that the witness was familiar with all of the events that were going on in Sarajevo. And in order to put to him these documents so they can be admitted, I don't think he is limited to asking him a broad question but can show him the document and ask how that tallies with his understanding of the situation. Unfortunately, because the document is not in Serbian, he has to read it to the witness otherwise the witness wouldn't appreciate its contents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: About there are other reports of the battle-field, there are a lot of reports, it seems that another battle-field was active. That was --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: It was my interpretation not to read the entire paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it was unnecessary and leading as well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I apologise, but in order to save some time because the full paragraph talks about other battle-fields. Can it be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll allow the question about Sarajevo. I'm not sure if the witness has answered the question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, he wasn't able to put in an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, the information about the combat in and around Sarajevo contained here, is it consistent with your own experience?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The news reported on by SRNA, I believe, is accurate. It also serves to confirm my own testimony to the effect that there was an offensive launched against the Serb positions and forces in every corner of every municipality of the Serb Sarajevo day and night. This specifically refers to the Herzegovina Corps which was under heavy artillery attack by the Muslim forces. They used the heaviest of calibres. They used sniper fire, and in that they were particularly dangerous and skilful. They had quite a few sharpshooters. The sniper fire was making the lives of civilians in Grbavica and other urban areas particularly difficult. Those who were in the area of Herzegovina Corps around Trnovo and Treskavica, aside from infantry attacks, they were under constant artillery fire from the Muslim forces with all types of calibre. There was also mortar fire, as can be seen here, et cetera. In that particular area I said that this was the point where the Herzegovina Corps and the SRK were linked up. This is where the MUP forces were present and they were resubordinated to the VRS. There was a great effort to prevent the Serb lines from being broken through and falling because that would have resulted in a large exodus and massacre of the civilian population in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D3758, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1D9125, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honours, I'm going to object again. There was some discussion, as I said, about what the focus would have been during this time when he was meeting with Mr. Karadzic. I don't think that that justifies a re-direct which includes - as Mr. Robinson basically admitted just a few pages earlier in the transcript - an opportunity to shove in a whole bunch of documents that they chose not to put in in direct on the Sarajevo front. He's made his point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Mr. Karisik, if you could excuse yourself for a moment. We need to discuss something in your absence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: During the cross-examination the witness, when asked by you about the Srebrenica event, he said he didn't know because he was involved in the Sarajevo front. Is it not legitimate on the part of the Defence to put something about Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I agree that it does, Your Honour, and that's what I said in the beginning. But what I don't think it does justify and is improper, goes beyond the scope of the re-direct for the cross, is to go into everything this witness knows about Sarajevo and to do a full Sarajevo direct which they chose not to do in the beginning. I didn't cross him on what was going on in Sarajevo. The witness has said, "I focused on Sarajevo," and they've shown him some documents which I didn't object to. But I think we're now going way beyond the scope of what's triggered by the cross, and it's just an effort to now put in a lot of media articles that they didn't make as part of the statement -- well, some that were probably but were excluded because they weren't discussed and weren't dealt with live in the beginning, which is the way it should have been handled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Really, we had no intention of even discussing this topic until Mr. Nicholls' cross-examination when -- now we're trying to corroborate the fact what the witness said about being engaged in Sarajevo, that there was a lot going on there. But if -- we're also concerned because we want to basically go through the time through, let's say, the 19th or the 20th when prisoners were being executed and events in Srebrenica were happening. But if the Prosecution would agree that those articles can be admitted, we'd have a few more of them. That would be a good compromise for us because it would save us some time and then they wouldn't -- we wouldn't have to put questions about the events in Sarajevo to the witness. So if they're willing to agree that the remaining articles for this period can be admitted, perhaps that's the best solution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's the crux of the Prosecution's objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I was just going to say that I thought their objection was he's getting into too many details about Sarajevo. This way we can avoid his knowledge of those details and yet make our point.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I am objecting to the articles coming in. Of course I don't agree to that. The other point is, it's not even a real contradiction of what my cross was. I never said you didn't discuss anything about Sarajevo. I never said nothing was going on in Sarajevo. I never said there was no combat in Sarajevo in my cross. What I -- the point of my cross was that it -- I was putting to him that it was incredible that during the entire Srebrenica operation you don't discuss it once. His response was: Well, I was so focused on Sarajevo the whole time. That's why I didn't object in the beginning to some point showing that there were things going on in Sarajevo. But I don't believe I've opened the door now to the Sarajevo case for half of July coming in through this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, the Chamber is of the view that you dealt with Sarajevo thing already sufficiently, so I would like you to move on to another topic. Shall we bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. While the witness is being brought in, I'd like to say this: The reports reaching the general public day in and day out show the importance of Srebrenica at the time. It was marginal. There were a great many other things that were important.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is not evidence. I'm explaining why this is important. Mr. Nicholls did manage to have another document admitted by advancing additional submissions; why shouldn't I do the same?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You could have used some documents already in evidence instead of tendering the news articles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please move on to another topic, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will. But just for the sake of the transcript, Your Excellencies, I do not consider these to be newspaper articles but news agency reports. Can we have that document that we had on our screens admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It was not dealt with, was it? So please move on to another topic, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karisik, my apologies. I forgot the sitting schedule I referred to earlier on, but we'll stick to it from now on. Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bear with me for a moment, please. I have to change the order of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, sir, I'll have one final question for you, then. I've had to change the way I imagine my examination. General, did you ever report to me about any unlawful killings or executions in Srebrenica after its fall?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I give up on all the other questions that I had, Your Excellency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. That concludes your evidence, Mr. Karisik. On behalf of the Chamber, I thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Please have a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could call your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Our next witness is Nenad Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could the witness make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Deronjic. Please be seated and make yourself comfortable.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you commence your evidence, Mr. Deronjic, I must draw your attention to a certain rule of evidence that we have here at the International Tribunal, that is, Rule 90(E). Under this rule you may object to answering any question from Mr. Karadzic, the Prosecution, or even from the Judges if you believe that your answer might incriminate you in a criminal offence. In this context, "incriminate" means saying something that might amount to an admission of guilt for a criminal offence or saying something that might provide evidence that you might have committed a criminal offence. However, should you think that an answer might incriminate you and, as a consequence, you refuse to answer the question, I must let you know that the Tribunal has the power to compel you to answer the question. But in that situation, the Tribunal would ensure that your testimony compelled under such circumstances would not be used in any case that might be laid against you for any offence, save and except the offence of giving false testimony. Do you understand what I have just told you, Mr. Deronjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us make a pause between my question and your answers. Can you tell us if you testified before this Tribunal in the Blagojevic case?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did testify in the Blagojevic case before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the course of proofing, did you have an opportunity to listen to the recording of your evidence in that case?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did have that opportunity and I did listen to my testimony in the Blagojevic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does the transcript and its contents faithfully reflect what you said at the time or do you need to make any corrections?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: It fully reflects what I said. That said, I would have a correction to make. It has to do with my statement about the engagement of the 2nd Company of the special police unit in Srebrenica. I said at the time that the entire 2nd Company of the special police unit was engaged in the territory of Srebrenica; however, not the entire company was there. One part of the 2nd Company was in Srebrenica, whereas the other part of the 2nd Company of the special police unit was deployed elsewhere. I don't know where.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up 1D6909.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Besides that correction about the 2nd Company and its one half being in Srebrenica and its other half being somewhere else, does everything else faithfully reflect what you stated?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Everything else that I stated at the time faithfully reflects what I meant, so that would be that, that would be my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I were to put the same questions to you today, the same as were put to you by the Defence, the Prosecutor, and the Judges, would your answers essentially be the same?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Essentially, my answers would be the same as I provided in the Blagojevic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm tendering this transcript into evidence pursuant to Rule 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, we would actually be tendering this transcript under seal and it would contain the confidential version and there's a public transcript that has been uploaded in e-court as 1D09041.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you are tendering two versions, public version and confidential version?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And you're tendering any associated exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. There's one associated exhibit, 1D6946 and it was not on our 65 ter list. We would ask that it be added as we hadn't made a final decision as to what documents we would use with this witness at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Presiding Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Where is that log-book referred to in the transcript page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it it's to be -- 8194?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I see the mistake, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objection, Mr. Costi?

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit both versions of the transcript as well as the associated exhibits. Shall we assign the numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the under seal transcript will be Exhibit D3759, under seal. The public version will be Exhibit D3760. And 1D6946 will be Exhibit D3761.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And now I'm going to read a short summary of Mr. Deronjic's evidence contained in the transcript that has just been admitted. [In English] Nenad Deronjic is the first of three witnesses who will testify about scheduled incident E1, the alleged execution of 15 Bosnian Muslim men from Srebrenica on the bank of the Jadar River near Konjevic Polje on the morning of 13th of July, 1995. Prosecution Witness KDZ065, whose evidence was admitted in this case in writing as Exhibit P336, claims that Nenad Deronjic was the one -- was one of the four persons who committed that execution. Mr. Deronjic, who worked as a police officer in Bratunac, has testified that he never participated in any such execution and that he was not even working in the Konjevic Polje area on 13th of July, 1995. He has testified that beginning in the afternoon of 12th of July, 1995, he was assigned to work in the Srebrenica police station and was working in Srebrenica on 13th of July at the time Witness KDZ065 claimed -- claims he was in Konjevic Polje. At that moment I don't have questions for Mr. Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just have one comment. I should have objected before. The accused started introduction of this witness by making comments about this is the first of three witnesses. That is clearly not part of his summary and not part of the testimony of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Deronjic, your evidence in this case has been admitted in writing, and that is through your testimony in the earlier case in lieu of your oral testimony. Now you will be cross-examined by the representative of the Office of the Prosecutor. Yes, Mr. Costi.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, and everyone else in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Deronjic. Now, in your written testimony just admitted you said that you left Konjevic Polje and went to Srebrenica on the 12th of July; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, you also said that in Srebrenica you were tasked with regular police activities; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And in your testimony you also agreed that in Srebrenica there was no combat activity from the 12th of July on; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: In the centre of Srebrenica where I was there was none.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Finally, you also agreed in your testimony that by the afternoon or evening hours of the 12th of July, Muslims from Srebrenica were breaking through the area around Konjevic Polje, Ravni Buljim, and you agree that that was a combat zone; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I don't remember having stated that about combat activities in that region. There may have been some, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Well, let me read you back what you said at page 34 of your Blagojevic testimony and on line 9. You were asked: "Well, on the afternoon/evening hours of the 12th of July, Muslims from the Srebrenica -- from Srebrenica, armed Muslims, were breaking through the area around Konjevic Polje and that was a combat zone. Were you aware of that?" And you answered: "Yes." And then you were asked: "So you're aware that Konjevic Polje has become a combat zone shortly after the time that you left it. So you must have been relieved to have been able to get the assignment to go down to Srebrenica, which was not a combat zone?" And your answer was: "You could put it that way." So do you agree that you said - and you stand by what you said - that in the area of Konjevic Polje at that time there was combat activity; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: It is possible that there was a combat zone there; however, during that period of time, if I had been given a task to go to Konjevic Polje I should have gone there. If I had been ordered to go there, I would have had to obey that order. I would have had to go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: I was not asking whether you were ordered to go there. I was simply asking - as soon as I have your attention. I was simply asking whether you knew that there was combat activity at that time in that part, in the area of Konjevic Polje? And you answered "yes" in the Blagojevic case. So do you stand by what you said in the Blagojevic case?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what you mean. How do you mean that I knew? Nobody told me anything. I was not in charge. I was not a commander. Nobody informed me about any combat activities. Nobody was accountable to me. I was just an ordinary policeman who did his job. As a regular policeman, who was it that should have informed me about combat activities ongoing there? I suppose that there were combat activities going on there because the troops were headed in that direction. They passed through that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Very well. You suppose that there was combat activity. You sort of stand by what you said in the Blagojevic case, do you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Well, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now can I have now just been admitted D3761, which is the July log-book of the Bratunac SJB.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, you discuss this document to a large extent in your testimony in Blagojevic, so I don't want to spend too much time on this and I would just, mainly for the benefit of the Chamber, repeat a few basic points about it, of your testimony about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: That shouldn't be this one. It should be at P -- it should be an Exhibit Number, the one just we admitted. It used to be 65 ter 1 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: D -- [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Here we are. So if we can just see the first page for the moment and turn it.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, the first row indicates the date of the month; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now if we go to then the second page, you see that the -- one, two, three, four -- the fifth row, it is you, that is your name; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, unfortunately we cannot see the first page now, but if we look from -- towards the end it says Srebrenica SJB Srebrenica. Right? Towards the right side in correspondent of your role?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: This indicates that you were at the SJB Srebrenica from - and tell me if I'm wrong - the 21st of July onward? This document says that you were applied to the SJB -- to the SJB Srebrenica from the 21st of July onward; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: That's correct. From the 21st I was assigned to the police station in Srebrenica which is where I did my police job. That's where I was deployed. That's where I was assigned to.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Very well. So if we go backwards, the nine days before, again on your role we can read bd, bd, bd for each day until one day when it says 08 BD. And these are the days from the 12th of July to the 20th of July; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And you explained in your testimony in Blagojevic BD stands for combat operation; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, if we can go back to the first page, and before we go there, you said in your statement, in your testimony, that Mirko Peric, a colleague of yours from Bratunac was in Konjevic Polje on the 11th and 12th of July; right? Sir, before reading, my question is: Is it correct that you testified that Mirko Peric was in Konjevic Polje on the 11th and 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Mirko Peric was in Konjevic Polje. I don't know whether he was at the check-point or somewhere else --

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: But he was in Konjevic Polje --

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: -- but he was in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Very well. Now, can you tell me if we look at this document again, you see that Mirko Peric is one of the names. And if you can look at the 11th and 12th of July, can you tell this Court what the document indicates?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: It says "bd" here for the 12th, that's combat operations. And then we see one, two, three, four, five, and then 18, and then combat operations on the 18th, 19th, and 20th, and 21st.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So do you agree that while he was in Konjevic Polje, Mirko Peric, on the 11th and 12th of July, he was marked on this log-book as "bd," combat operation; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I would not like to comment on Mirko Peric. However, if you insist, I still don't know what I can say about him. I know what I did, where I was. I don't want to say anything about Mirko Peric. I really don't feel comfortable.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: I'm asking you to talk about the document, not about Mirko Peric. Does the document say on the 11th and 12th of July, Mirko Peric was in combat operation, bd? It's very simple.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: That's what it says in this document. As I've just told you on the 11th and --

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Thank you. You answered my question. Now, as you said in your statement and your testimony, you were a member of the 2nd Company of the Zvornik PJP; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And you said that you were activated as a member of the 2nd PJP around 12 -- of the 12th of July; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Can we have Exhibit P5136, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, you will see appearing on your screen a document which is a daily events report of the Zvornik CJB of the 14th of July. Now, if we go to the second page and if we read point 5 of the second page, point 5 says: "Due to infiltration of enemy military formations from Srebrenica into the zone of the Zvornik CJB and areas of Konjevic Polje - Cerska, Han Pogled, Dzafin Kamen, Snagovo, Marcici and other places at risk, the 1st, 2nd, 5th, and 6th Companies of the Zvornik CJB are engaged. In co-ordinated action with the police from Doboj, Bijeljina, and Pale, as well as the VRS, they are laying ambushes." Now, do you agree that this document says that the 2nd PJP, so your company, was engaged in combat activities; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: According to this document, it says in it that it is correct, i.e., that the 2nd Company was engaged in the tasks indicated herein.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And there is no indication in this report that the 2nd PJP was engaged in regular police activity in Srebrenica; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: You're right; however, I've just explained to you what I did and that was that one part of the 2nd Company - which may be proven in several ways - and that is one half of the 2nd Company was in Srebrenica and I was with them. And it is also possible that the other half or the rest of the 2nd Company was in this area. This document was shown to me when I testified in the Blagojevic case as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Let me show you another document that was also shown to you before which is P04935.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And here we need the B/C/S page 2 and the English page 1 at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And again at point 5 it explains what you just said in a way, so: "... acting upon President Karadzic ... which was conveyed to us today, the 2nd Company of the Zvornik PJP shall be dispatched to Srebrenica with the task to secure facilities of vital importance." And then it continues and it says below: "A platoon of this company will lie ambush in Ravni Buljim since the Muslim group was spotted fleeing along that axis." So we do know where the other half of the 2nd PJP was and my question to you is quite simple. I'm suggesting you were part of that platoon who was deployed arresting and capturing Muslims in the area of Ravni Buljim, including Konjevic Polje. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: This is not correct. It will never be correct. It is absolutely not correct. Me and my company, which consisted of two platoons, we were engaged, but we never moved from the centre of Srebrenica which stretched from the football-pitch and the check-points that were set up at the entrance into the city. We were there for the whole of the nine days. We never moved from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, let me try to explore a little bit more the steps of your assignment to the Srebrenica SJB.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Can I have 65 ter 04059, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, you will see appearing on your screen an order from the -- Dragomir Vasic, head of the Zvornik CJB on 15 of July. Now, this order is sent to the Srebrenica SJB, and at point 5, which should be probably on page 2 of the B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may be of assistance, I would say that this is not correct. It starts on page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, at point 5, and I read the English: "In the course of the day, the chief of Srebrenica SJB, Petko Pavlovic, will send the chief of the Zvornik CJB a list of policemen from Srebrenica who are currently working in Zvornik CJB stations." And then at point 8 it says: "The chief of the Srebrenica SJB must urgently assemble a strong police squad from policemen from all stations of the centre who are originally from Srebrenica." Now, you said in your testimony that you were applied to the Srebrenica SJB because you used to be a policeman from Srebrenica; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: That's right. However, on the 12th I was sent to carry out a task as a member of the 2nd Company of the Zvornik PJP. After the completion of that mission I was transferred to the police station in Srebrenica because that's the police station that I had worked in before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So do you agree that in this document the Zvornik CJB is in the process of selecting or identifying the policemen that will then be assigned to the Srebrenica SJB? I'm not asking whether you were there on the 12th or not. I'm asking this document confirms what you said and is plain -- and the Zvornik CJB is in the process of identifying the policemen from Srebrenica; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I agree with that. Why wouldn't I?

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I have this document admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6427.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: I would like to see another document, 65 ter 25306 [Realtime transcript read in error "25036"].

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, this is an information report from the Srebrenica SJB to the Zvornik CJB on the 16th of July and it's signed by Petko Pavlovic, which is the chief of Srebrenica SJB.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you check the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Let me check.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I have it on my screen 25306.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Yeah. You had -- should be 25306. I'm sorry. I must have read the wrong number, 306. Yeah. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, if we look at this document, it said: "Pursuant to your dispatch mentioned above ... we hereby submit to you a list of police employees who worked at the Srebrenica SJB until the eruption of the war ..." And if you look at number 3, is your name, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So do you agree that here, the Srebrenica SJB, Pavlovic is responding to the document we saw one second ago and is providing him with a list of policemen that used to work in the Srebrenica SJB before the beginning of the war. Right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And could we have this document admitted as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6428, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now the third document I would like to show you is 25091.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And this one is the order of the Zvornik CJB on 16th of July, which reads: "Due to the need for establishment of a police station in Srebrenica, upon its liberation, and pursuant to the approval of the Deputy Minister of the Interior, I hereby issue the following order. "The below listed policemen who had previously worked at the Srebrenica SJB are to be sent immediately, by the 21st of July, 1995, at the latest, to the Srebrenica SJB, where the station chief, in co-ordination with the officer in charge of the Zvornik CJB, shall assign them to their duties and tasks." And number 3, it's your name, Nenad Deronjic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So we saw the three passages. At the end, the CJB finally ordered you to be sent and to report to Srebrenica, so -- correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Finally, one last document, which is 65 --

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, I will ask this document to be admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6429, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: One last which is 65 ter 25304.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, this is a MUP administrative instruction issued on the 18 June 1996 for administrative purposes. And it reads: "Pursuant to paragraph 3, Article 73 of the State Administration Law ... and Articles 12 and 15 of the Employment Relation Law, the minister of internal affairs of Republika Srpska issued this decision. "Nenad ... Deronjic is to be assigned to the duties and tasks of the police officer in Zvornik CJB Srebrenica police station." And then it continues: "... commencing on the 21st of July, 1995." So also this document, you agree, confirms that you were reporting and submitted to the Srebrenica SJB from the 21st July 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Correct. This decision confirms that as of the 21st of July, 1995, I was to be transferred to the Srebrenica public security station to work as a policeman. As I said, I was discharging my duties in Srebrenica between the 12th and the 21st.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, can I have this document admitted, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6430, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Do you agree, don't you, that all the documents that we have seen so far, starting from the log-book all the way to the administrative instruction from 1996, indicate that you were in combat operation from the 12th of July until the 20th of July, and then you were in Srebrenica from the 21st of July on within the Srebrenica SJB. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: That is correct, but if I may clarify. You're trying to say that I was in combat between the 12th and the 21st, which means that you think that I wasn't in Srebrenica but elsewhere engaged in combat. If you engage a PJP company, regardless of what the assignment is, they always state "combat operation" without going into any specifics. The simplest way is just to enter the phrase "combat operation," which means that this specific company was engaged in doing specific jobs. I see what you're trying to say, that the company where I was --

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: I'm not trying to saying anything. I'm saying that this document indicate only that you were in combat operation, and then -- then you were at the police in Srebrenica from the 21st. That before that, that is your words, saying that you were in the part of the 2nd PJP that in Srebrenica, but I'm suggesting that you were not in that part but in Konjevic Polje together with Mirko Peric who is also marked in the log-book as bd, combat operation, on the same days. So I'm asking you directly then: Were you in Konjevic Polje during those days, not necessarily applied to the check-point, but in Konjevic Polje with the 2nd PJP?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No. I explained where I was and what I was doing in the period between the 12th and the 21st which is the time where I never left the inner part of Srebrenica town.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: I believe it is probably time for the break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So we can break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll have a break for 45 minutes and resume at quarter past 1.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.31 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Costi. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Can I have 65 ter 24716A, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Deronjic, there is just one last document I want to discuss with you, and you had discussed this document already in your Blagojevic testimony. It is a Srebrenica SJB log-book.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I'm afraid it hasn't been released, Mr. Costi.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Can we move on and get it uploaded later? Okay. I move to the next question and then -- can we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, I just -- I think that that document might have been released under 24716 without an A, but if you check that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, as I was saying, you discussed this document also during your Blagojevic testimony, and apart from all the other documents that we have seen till now, this is the only one that might suggest that you were in Srebrenica on the 12th and the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now can we go on page 4 of the English and the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, if you look at this page, at the bottom, it says that you on the 12th of July were on duty from 19 hours to 24 hours. Right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And if we go to page 6 of both B/C/S and English, it says that you were on duty on the 13th from 7 -- 19 hours to 7, so from the evening of the 13th until the morning of the 14th; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And if we go to page 7 of the B/C/S and 8 of the English, we see that you were on duty between the -- from the 7 in the morning of the 13th until the 7 in the afternoon of the 13th, even it is the following page it still refers on the 13th of July. So in other words, on the -- after being on shift during the night of the 12th, according to this log-book you had a 24-hour shift from 7 in the morning of the 13th all the way to the 7 in the morning of the 14th. Is this correct? You had a 24-hour shift after a 12-hour or a seven- or eight-hour shift the night before?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, if we look at this entry on the B/C/S side, if we can zoom in a little bit, at the one on -- the one that we have in front of us now, you will see that the time between 07 to 19 of the 13 of July has been altered, and this is the time when you were seen in Konjevic Polje shooting at Muslim prisoners; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I don't know on what basis you claim that I was shooting --

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: I will get to that.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: -- how was I seen from 7 to 19 --

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: I will get to tell you the basis upon which in one minute. But what I'm asking you now is: Do you agree, as you did in Blagojevic, that this has been altered?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: One can see that this had been altered, but I don't know who did that. I don't know who had access to this document. So anyone could have done it. You can see here that it says 07 to 19 corrected obviously. I don't know who did it or why and who had access to this document. Let me just tell you one more thing if possible. At the beginning, on the cover you can see that there is something written and this is my handwriting. You can ask a graphology expertise to be done on this, but I can confirm that this is my handwriting and you can compare it with my signature if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: We can go on the first page is what he said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is my signature, roster for Srebrenica SJB, 12.07.1995, and beneath you can see my signature and a graphologist can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And why is your signature on the first page of this SJB Srebrenica log-book?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. It just happened like that. There is no significance to that. I perhaps just signed it. It's irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So let's move on to another topic, or rather, to the same topic from another perspective.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Can we go, please, into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are you tendering that?

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry, Your Honour. Yes, we tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we don't object to this. We think this is an important document. But I would like to ask at this point so we can understand, is it the Prosecution's case that, as they have spent the last half an hour establishing that he was not in Srebrenica at all during this period from the 12th to the 21st, and if that's the case, what is the explanation for all of the unaltered entries in this log-book for 12, 13, 14, et cetera? I think it would help us to know that so we can determine what other witnesses, if any, are necessary to bring to establish this point which is very important to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Costi, can you assist us?

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Yeah. Your Honour, our case is that the witness was in Konjevic Polje at the time on the 13th of July. Rather than that -- and that from the 21st indeed was assigned to the Srebrenica SJB. As to his whereabouts in the meanwhile, it is not clear or known to us but what counts is our case he was there and his effort to show that he was in Srebrenica are not successful.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: But all of these entries for the dates -- besides the one that's altered, show that he's in Srebrenica during all that time and that's inconsistent with the Prosecution's case that they've been putting to him so far, that he didn't go to Srebrenica until the 21st. So I would like to know whether or not it's the Prosecution's case that he was in Srebrenica for some of that time or that this book is somehow inaccurate or falsified in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure it's appropriate to discuss this in the presence of the witness, but I don't -- have difficulty following your submission that it would be inconsistent with the Prosecution's case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, the Prosecution was showing all of these documents at the beginning of the cross-examination, showing that it was only on the 21st that he was assigned to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, just a second. Why don't we excuse the witness for the moment. Mr. Deronjic, if you could excuse yourself for the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let me ask you, Mr. Robinson, simply. Is it your case that it's impossible to go to Konjevic Polje while posted or while being in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then what is your point, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Our point is that during this time he was assigned in Srebrenica and not in Konjevic Polje. So it's less likely that he would have gone to Konjevic Polje. The Prosecution seems to be arguing that he was assigned to the part of this company who was in combat in the area around Konjevic Polje. And so they presented what I consider to be two conflicting sets of documentation to establish that, one, that he was not part of the group of that company that went to Srebrenica from the 12th; and the other that -- this log-book showing that he was in Srebrenica from the 12th. So I would like to know which of those two the -- what is the Prosecution's case as to that because we can bring the chief and the other people from Srebrenica if it's disputed that he was actually one of the men who were working there from the 12th. So it's helpful to us to know exactly what the Prosecution's case is on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Costi.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: I would repeat more or less what I just said. Our case is that he was there on the 13th in Konjevic Polje in the morning. Whether at that point he wasn't at that check-point anymore, whether he was assigned to Srebrenica and he drove to Konjevic Polje to commit the crimes is not up to us to say it. Our case is that he was there on the 13th and we believe that it was fair to the Defence to -- and to the witness to put him also this document that we consider, generally speaking, are reliable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You are not arguing that, other than this altered part, it was made up or fabricated?

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: We argue that in general this document is not unreliable. We don't think it's all fabricated, I agree, Your Honour, but the fact there has been a change at that time shows that the whole document is unreliable in light of all the other documents that we highlighted before.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: But if I could just ask what was the point, then, of showing him all these documents to show that he was not in Srebrenica before the 21st of July?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Costi, can we hear your reply to Mr. Robinson's last point, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I think the point was to make clear that the formal appointment to the SJB in Srebrenica had been on the 21st. And this is also relevant to the testimony of other witnesses that are going to come in the next days. The second point is that, in any event, the core of the documents that we've seen only unequivocally indicated that he was there from the 21st, while there is a gap of time where he was with the PJP, 2nd PJP. He could have been in one position ambushing Muslims or he could have been with the 2nd PJP deployed apparently in Srebrenica. Now, there is one document which suggests indeed that he was in Srebrenica for at least some of the time. And we believed that although it's not reliable and it doesn't outweigh the rest of the documents it was fair to put it to the witness. It would have been misleading the Chamber if we had just not bring this document up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber sees no difficulty with the line of questions of the Prosecution. We'll continue. Shall we bring in the witness. While the witness is being brought in, the Chamber has considered the issue of Mr. Beara's and Miletic -- General Miletic's evidence. In the circumstances, the Chamber has decided to postpone those witnesses, pending the outcome of the Tolimir appeal to the Appeals Chamber on the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I will come back to Keserovic's evidence after this witness's evidence is over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue, Mr. Costi.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Can we move, please, in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Have we admitted this one? Yes, shall we give the number for this?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6431, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How many pages should we admit, Mr. Costi? Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: It should be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Cover page and relevant part --

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Yeah, right, eight pages -- the English is eight pages and the B/C/S should be seven pages, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So we'll admit those pages translated?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those were 4 and 6, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: It was 4, 6, and 8 of the English and 4, 6, and 7 of the B/C/S, but we also discussed the first -- the cover page, so even page 1 probably should be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes. Shall we go to private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Deronjic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The representative of the Prosecution, when questioning me today, said that this part of the PJP company completely went to Konjevic Polje in order to commit these killings. Now when you showed me this document the only thing that you pointed out are the alterations next to my name. What about the rest of them? What about the others? Does that mean that I was the only one present there? Because I see that the only alteration made was next to my name. What about the other names? Are you claiming that they were there as well or are you saying that I was the only one who was there?

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Let me move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Miroslav Deronjic is your cousin, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, a distant cousin. We bear the same family name but we are not close family.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, you gave an interview to the OTP on the 12th March 2001 and there you said that you joined the Bratunac police station in April 1992. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, you are aware that on the 9th of May, 1992, the village of Glogova was attacked by Bratunac TOs and other Serb forces including police from the Bratunac police station. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I didn't participate in that, so I don't want to give any comments on it if I don't have to. I wasn't there when it was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Right. Let's start from the beginning of the process that led to the attack to Glogova. So the collection of weapons, as you may be aware, weapons were collected from Muslim villages including Glogova. On the 7th of May, you were part of the Serb delegation who collected weapons from villages from Glogova. I'm talking about 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. I didn't go to Glogova at all, nor did I collect any weapons, nor did I go to these Muslims' houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 25333, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, this is a statement that a protected witness in the Milosevic case, B-1701, gave to the Prosecution in March 2002. He describes -- he was from Glogova, he describes all the process that they went through. And at paragraph 10 -- I'm sorry, paragraph 10 which is page 4 of the English and page 4 of the B/C/S. And I start reading. He talks about this negotiation that took place on the 7th of May in the primary school, but I would like more specifically now to state that they took place in front of Mehmed Ibisevic's house which is close to the school. The negotiator on the Muslim side was Ahmo Ibisevic from Glogova, whereas I remember that it was Mico Milosavljevic, and not Milutin as I state in my previous statement, who was with Nenad Deronjic from Magasici village on the Serbian side. The villagers surrendered some weapons that day on the promise that the village would not be attacked, but I surrendered my hunting rifle the next day." So my question for you is: You were part of the Serb delegation during those negotiations where you asked the weapon to be given to you and you promised that Glogova would not be attacked; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: That's not correct. I wasn't a negotiator at all. I can't obviously reason with you. I was never given a managing role by anyone to be in charge of anything. I was an ordinary --

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Let's forget the word --

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: -- policeman. How can I explain to you that I wasn't a platoon commander --

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Let's forget the word --

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Who would be the one to place me in charge of any negotiations?

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Let's forget about the word "negotiation." Were you together with Mico Milosavljevic on the 7th of May, meeting Muslims from Glogova and collecting from them weapons with the promise they would not be attacked?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't there. I can't even recall at this time who Mico Milosavljevic is. I wasn't in Glogova at all. At all.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Can I please have now 65 ter 25330.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, this is another statement from another Muslim that used to live in Glogova, and this one is actually talking about the attack that took place on the 9th of May. He said that he was hiding in the woods and from there he was witnessing what was happening in some part of Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And if we can go to English page 4 and B/C/S page 4 as well, and in English it is where it starts with "shortly after," whereas the B/C/S is the last two paragraphs of page 4. But I'll read it for the record: "Shortly after that I saw another group of about 15 soldiers walking up the road from the direction of Bratunac. I could see that Miroslav Deronjic and his cousin Nenad Deronjic were among them. They walked past the mosque, they came right up to the bridge. There they stopped and started talking with the group of soldiers already there. All of a sudden everything got a little quiet. I could see that Miroslav Deronjic hugged some of the soldiers there. He was dressed up in a camouflage uniform and he was wearing a green beret. "I had known Miroslav Deronjic very well ..." and then it explains why. Last line: "Similarly, I knew Nenad Deronjic quite well as he was also from the same village of Magasici."

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And my question for you is: You were in Glogova on the 9th of May together with your cousin Miroslav Deronjic during the attack?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. I wasn't in Glogova at all at the time. I wasn't there at all. Can I just explain one thing to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: The man who gave this statement, I know him well. A year ago I went to obtain a document for him from the municipality. I was on good terms with him and his father. I obtained a piece of paper that he needed and sent to him through his father. So I know this man - I won't say his name - know him well. I obtained a document for him in the municipality and sent it to him through his father --

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So you're saying --

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: -- I wasn't in Glogova in this period of time at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So you are saying that here we have another witness again that is lying seeing you where you were not?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I wasn't there. I'm telling you I know this man well. He's a neighbour of mine, and I told you that it was just recently that I got a document for him. I know his father and I see his father every other day. I'm in contact with him.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To avoid confusion, can we ask the Prosecutor to show us where the house of this witness was because we can tell that he was from the village of Magasici. So where is that house? Is it in Glogova? Where was it that he saw what he states here?

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think we need to go into these details. Although it's not a protected witness, I don't think it's necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't follow. Just a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is this witness protected?

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: No, he's not. But at the same time, I don't think it would be advisable to provide this information although because irrelevant in terms of his testimony because he says in the testimony that he was hiding in the woods so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, no, I'm asking. This witness's name could be revealed to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Yes it can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Yes, it can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you remember his father's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I read -- yes, I know his name. I'm in touch with his father every other day, either in the town of Bratunac or I go to his home in Glogova. I tell you, it was roughly a year ago that I obtained a piece of paper for this gentleman here who gave this statement in the municipality and I sent it to him through his father.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So this witness is lying, the other witness was lying. Now, your cousin Miroslav Deronjic, during his testimony in his own case on the 30th of September, 2003, at page 68 he was asked who was present during the attack. And he said that you were among those present.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I wasn't in Glogova at the time. Now, what they stated and how, I can't tell anyone what they should be stating. I wasn't there in that period. I think that I was even away from the police force for a period of time. I had some family business that I had to attend to. I don't know if it was in that period of time or later.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I have just one last question which is you said in an interview to the MUP of Republika Srpska on the 22nd of April, 2003, you were discussing the events in Srebrenica in 1995 and you were talking about the Muslims what moved from Potocari and then you were asked: "Were you aware that Muslim men were killed along the way?" And your answer was: "I was not aware of it at that time but I heard some stories to that effect later." So my question to you is: This was 2003. When did you first hear of mass execution, if you've ever heard of mass execution, taking place after the fall of Srebrenica? So basically let me split it in two, two questions. Have you ever heard of mass execution of Muslim prisoners after the fall of Srebrenica; and if yes, when?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Of course I heard it, but I can't tell you when it was. I did hear about the executions, but I can't set a precise time.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Are we talking about hours? Weeks? Months? Years?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: A longer period, but I can't really be more precise than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And you heard about it after the war? Before the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: After the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: I don't have any further questions. I think I have a few minutes left, but I don't need more time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, do you have any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Excellency. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deronjic, let's start from these freshest issues. The two individuals, father and son, did they file a criminal report against you? Did they testify against you? Was there some sort of legal action taken against you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: There was no legal action taken by them against me. I told you that I'm on good terms with the family, that I'm in touch with the father on a daily basis. Let me repeat, I recently obtained a piece of paper for him that I sent through his father.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were they called elsewhere in Bosnia to give statements concerning yourself?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of it and they didn't tell me anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you are given a task somewhere -- or, rather, first of all, can you explain to us what the difference is between regular policing duties and the assignment given within the PJP?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: When a special police unit is being engaged, a dispatch and an order is sent by the public security centre in Zvornik and one proceeds to execute the given assignment. It was thus that we were deployed to the battle-field in Treskavica and elsewhere, where we were on the separation line in trenches. Likewise, we were dispatched to Srebrenica to put together a police station to prevent looting and theft and protect private properties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there any difference in terms of the salary paid out or the years of pensionable service calculated? Do these conditions apply equally to the regular policing duties and these assignments within the framework of the PJP?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Well, there are no special payments given. It was treated the same way as any other police duty would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When performing regular policing duties, would your spare time be any different from your engagement within the PJP? When were you given time for rest, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Of course there is a difference. In regular policing duties we have shifts of duty during which we are on patrol. And then, following our shift, we have a period of time set aside for rest. As for the special police unit, our engagement there was non-stop until we completed the assignment that we had initially been deployed for.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the procedure in terms of you being absent from your duty station during your engagement within the PJP?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Well, we were not allowed to be absent without leave. In case we needed to leave our position, we had to inform the company commander or the deputy commander of the company, who would then provide their consent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When on special duty within the PJP, where would you be listed as an employee? Let's specifically look at this case when between 12 and -- or even before the 12th at Konjevic Polje, where were you listed as employed up until the 21st of July?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: In this particular case, up until the 21st of July, I was employed with the public security station in Bratunac, where I received my salary and where I had certain duties. Between the 12th and the 21st, I was engaged through the special police unit on specific tasks in Srebrenica, whereas as of 21, I was given a document where I was transferred to the Srebrenica public security station and took up duties there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us what changed on the 21st of July?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: What changed on the 21st of July was that I was reassigned from the Bratunac public security station to the Srebrenica public security station, where I was given a document certifying my reassignment to that station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where did you receive your salary from up until the 20th and where after the 21st?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Up until the 21st it was from the Bratunac public security station, whereas following the 21st, I received my salary from the MUP through the Srebrenica public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 24716 now. I think that it's received its P number now. It was the last document that was adopted, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is it. Can we have page 6, please, in both versions. The next page then, please. We have the right page in the Serbian version. I'm not sure about the English, though. It should be some other page, I believe. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at the Serbian version. The gentlemen by the name of Obrenovic, what were the dates of his engagement?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Under 2, Darko Obrenovic worked from 7.00 a.m. until 7.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the next?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Miladin Gligic, under 3, worked from 7.00 a.m. until 7.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the last two persons, the same shift?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Stevanovic from 7.00 p.m. to 7.00 a.m., and the same applies to Markovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who was able to see you in Srebrenica on the 13th of July in the course of that day?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: First of all, who can confirm that we were there? It can be confirmed by my colleagues from the 2nd Company of the PJP, Darko Obrenovic, Miladin Gligic, Sredoje Vojic, Pavle Pelemis, Nebojsa Milanovic, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And can you tell us this. You have mentioned the distance between Srebrenica and Konjevic Polje. Can you repeat how far that is?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: The distance between Srebrenica and Konjevic Polje is 30 kilometres. Bratunac-Konjevic Polje is 21 kilometres and Bratunac-Srebrenica is another 10 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The Prosecutor suggests that you just popped over to kill some people and returned. How would you have been able to go there without permission? What kind of vehicle would you have used if you didn't have your commander's approval? Was there a regular bus line? Were there any bicycles you can borrow?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: There was no transportation at the time, there was nothing. I could not have been there at all, and I'm telling you the Prosecutor claims that the complete 2nd Company was in Konjevic Polje and then creates a problem because the time of service under my name was corrected. I don't know whether everybody is a problem or is it just me that is a problem in this work schedule.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Deronjic. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Deronjic, that concludes your evidence. On behalf of the Chamber, I thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are we ready to continue with the next witness, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. The next witness will be ready tomorrow morning. I excused him for the day so that he didn't have to wait around, and because we don't have a lot of other witnesses this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Coming back to the -- Mr. Keserovic's evidence. Given the circumstances, the Chamber is minded to have a short adjournment or postponement between his examination-in-chief and cross-examination. But the Chamber will see how it evolves, whether there's a possibility that we can continue directly with the cross. But we'll leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, can I just address a few other scheduling issues for this week to inform you. First of all, tomorrow we will have KW558 as scheduled, and the Prosecution has graciously agreed that we can have the examination of Witness Mirko Peric, even though he will be testifying earlier than the 48 hours between the time that we disclosed his final statement and the time he begins his testimony. So we anticipate having both of those witnesses tomorrow. Unfortunately, the next witness, Dragan Andan, who is arriving -- he couldn't arrive earlier than tomorrow. We scheduled a proofing with him tomorrow evening. But he has to listen to his testimony from the Stanisic and Zupljanin case which was very lengthy and we don't believe that it can be completed tomorrow. And so it is our anticipation that he would not be ready to testify until Friday morning, so I want to alert the Trial Chamber to that. This is not a conspiracy for me to have the 4th of July free, but that appears to be something that seems likely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Then we'll continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 3rd day of July, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.10 p.m.,
